study type: Observational study using a sibling-pair design with family fixed effects
outcome: Childhood obesity (BMI z-score at 2 and 5 years of age)
cohort: Children from the Linked the Collecting Electronic Nutrition Trajectory Data Using e-Records of Youth (CENTURY) Study (N = 55,058 at 2 years of age, N = 43,894 at 5 years of age)
finding: After accounting for unmeasured familial factors using a sibling-pair design, associations between breastfeeding initiation, cesarean delivery, prenatal smoking, and childhood obesity were attenuated and no longer significant.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with a higher BMI z-score in the full sample and sibling-only models but not in the fixed effects model.
